artworks.title: Ixion, King of the Lapiths, Deceived by Juno
artworks.description: Rubens' Louvre canvas stages the cloud-deception: Ixion embraces the false Juno — the Nephele/Nubes Zeus (or Hera) shaped — while the true goddess looks on. The cloud-mate who will mother Centaurus and the centaur brood stands at the hinge of Lapith desire and Tartarean punishment.

popCulture.title: Fabulae
popCulture.creator: Hyginus
popCulture.description: Hyginus names Nubes as Ixion's mate and mother of the centaur kind — the Latin cloud distinct from Nephele wife of Athamas.

popCulture.title: Ixion
popCulture.description: The king who lies with the cloud in Hera's likeness — father, with Nubes, of Centaurus and the wild Thessalian race.

popCulture.title: Centaurus (Greek mythology)
popCulture.description: Son of Ixion and the cloud — the ancestor who mates with Magnesian mares and fathers the Centaurs.

popCulture.title: Nephele
popCulture.description: Greek tradition often calls Ixion's cloud Nephele — carefully kept here distinct from Nephele mother of Phrixus and Helle.
